name: Plant street trees on open sites
sources: City Pretty local hedonic: 3,386 Westside sales 2022-24, block fixed effects; each street tree within 50 m +0.51% (95% CI 0.24-0.79) | LAMC 62.177 in-lieu fee: $1,945 per public-works tree incl. planting and 3-yr establishment | USFS / California street-tree costing: $52-79 per tree-year upkeep

name: Green a schoolyard (asphalt to trees and grass)
caveat: +1% is borrowed from passive parks; no schoolyard-specific price estimate exists.
sources: LAUSD 2023: $78.2M for seven campus exterior/greening packages (~$11.2M each, includes paving, fencing, ADA); LAUSD Greening Index 2022 (% green space by campus) | Crompton & Nicholls 2020 review: +8-10% adjacent to passive parks; small-park effect within ~100 m (Laszkiewicz 2022)

name: Clean and green vacant lots
caveat: Philadelphia costs; LA site control or land costs are not included.
sources: Lin, Jensen & Wachter 2023 (Philadelphia): +4.3% nearby after year 1 | Philadelphia LandCare: $1,500 initial / $300 a year per lot (2008$) | Branas et al. 2018 RCT: gun violence -29% in poor neighborhoods

name: Community garden
caveat: NYC effect; build cost assumed, land cost estimated.
sources: Voicu & Been 2008 (NYC): +1.5 pts at 1,000 ft, larger in poorer areas | Pasadena Parks Needs Assessment 2016: community garden $300k; LA RAP Hollywood rec center Phase II $16.5M + $2M contingency (2025)

name: Green alley (permeable paving, trees)
sources: Avalon Green Alley North phase II (2015): $1.83M

name: Cool pavement coating on hot streets
sources: Pacoima / Covina cool-pavement studies: surface -5 C, air -0.2 to -1.9 C; Middel 2020: midday radiant heat +4 C for pedestrians

name: Pocket park on a new lot
caveat: A passive-park premium, not measured for new quarter-acre parks; land cost is estimated.
sources: Crompton & Nicholls 2020 review: +8-10% adjacent to passive parks; small-park effect within ~100 m (Laszkiewicz 2022) | LA 50 Parks Initiative: 5,000-20,000 sq ft parks $250k-700k to develop, land extra | Albouy, Christensen & Sarmiento-Barbieri: park value falls where homicide risk is high

name: Renovate the nearby park (new playground, paths)
caveat: No matched renovation coefficient; the cost covers equipment and installation.
sources: Livy & Klaiber 2016: playground replacement among the most capitalized park upgrades; Brasington 2023: park-maintenance levy renewal +11.6% | Culver City, Culver West Alexander playground, Nov 2025: $759,353

name: Convert a tennis court to 4 pickleball courts
sources: Redondo Beach Alta Vista 2026: tennis resurfacing + 1 court to 4 pickleball $107,408; Cerritos 2 pickleball courts $134k | Minneapolis 2014 park-facility study: passive features add value; some active/skate facilities lower nearby values

name: Build 2 public tennis courts
sources: Redondo Beach Alta Vista 2026: tennis resurfacing + 1 court to 4 pickleball $107,408; Cerritos 2 pickleball courts $134k | Minneapolis 2014 park-facility study: passive features add value; some active/skate facilities lower nearby values

name: Build a public basketball court
sources: LA County PNA 2016: one full basketball court $436,250 | Minneapolis 2014 park-facility study: passive features add value; some active/skate facilities lower nearby values

name: Dog park
caveat: The dog-park study's coefficient was not recovered; +0.25% is an assumption.
sources: Castillo-Castillo et al. 2025 (Twin Cities): dog parks positively associated with nearby values (coefficient not recovered); Beverly Hills 2015 estimate $400-450k for a basic dog park

name: Public swimming pool
sources: LA County Hilda L. Solis Aquatic Center: $36.56M revised budget (Oct 2026); LA CAO 2022: $2.08M yearly O&M for the pool program (full per-pool O&M not recovered)

name: Splash pad
sources: LA RAP Juntos Park splash pad: $642,021 (2017)

name: Skate park
sources: LA County George Lane skate park (Quartz Hill): $2.1M for ~10,000 sq ft (2016); O&M not recovered | Minneapolis 2014 park-facility study: passive features add value; some active/skate facilities lower nearby values

name: Natural-grass sports field
sources: Sunnyvale 2023: natural-grass field $516,150 vs synthetic $2.03M; Culver City PNA field replacement $2.8M

name: Recreation center
sources: Pasadena Parks Needs Assessment 2016: community garden $300k; LA RAP Hollywood rec center Phase II $16.5M + $2M contingency (2025)

name: Park restroom and drinking fountains
sources: LA County Measure A: South LA replacement restroom building $990,000

name: Peak-hour bus lanes on the busy corridor
caveat: +0.5% is scaled down from full BRT; no study isolates bus lanes.
sources: Metro Wilshire bus lanes: $31.5M for 9.9 miles (2013); Culver City Robertson bus/bike lanes $1.22M (2025) | Metro Flower St bus lane: buses up to 30% faster | Beaudoin & Tyndall 2024 (Vancouver WA BRT): +5-7% home prices; Metro NoHo-Pasadena BRT $429M / 19 mi = $22.6M per mile; Vermont BRT $33.4M per mile

name: Bus rapid transit (stations, lanes, signal priority)
sources: Beaudoin & Tyndall 2024 (Vancouver WA BRT): +5-7% home prices; Metro NoHo-Pasadena BRT $429M / 19 mi = $22.6M per mile; Vermont BRT $33.4M per mile

name: New rail station (regional project, local share)
caveat: Shows this area's share of a far larger regional project.
sources: Debrezion, Pels & Rietveld 2007 meta-analysis: +4.2% residential within station area; Keeler & Stephens 2023 (LA Gold/Expo)

name: Bus shelters with shade at busy stops
sources: LA Sidewalk & Transit Amenities Program: provisional $180,842 per shelter (city memo, 2025)

name: Speed humps and traffic calming
caveat: Portland measured flow-reducing calming, not speed humps alone; hump cost is construction only.
sources: LADOT 2025: $5,958 per speed hump, up to 25-year life | Polloni 2019 (Portland): traffic calming that cuts flow 16% raises treated-street values ~1%

name: Safer crossings (bulb-outs, ramps, refuges)
sources: Santa Monica Blvd Safety Study 2026: ADA ramp $9,000; bulb-out $11,000-18,000 | FHWA: refuge islands -46% pedestrian crashes; road diets -29% crashes

name: Road diet with protected bike lanes
sources: Metro Wilshire bus lanes: $31.5M for 9.9 miles (2013); Culver City Robertson bus/bike lanes $1.22M (2025) | FHWA: refuge islands -46% pedestrian crashes; road diets -29% crashes

name: Repair broken sidewalks
sources: LA Controller 2021 sidewalk audit: $51 per sq ft incl. soft costs

name: Brighter pedestrian street lighting
caveat: The New York trial measured nighttime outdoor crime; only that share (~30%) is used.
sources: Chalfin et al. (NYC RCT): street lighting -36% nighttime outdoor index crime | LA Bureau of Street Lighting: ~$5,000 per 50-ft residential lot to build; ~$90 a year upkeep assessment | Schwartz, Susin & Voicu 2003 (NYC): 1% less violent crime -> +0.116% home prices

name: Security cameras at hot spots
sources: Cameron et al. 2008 (Hollywood and Jordan Downs cameras): no significant crime effect in LA; Piza et al. 2019 meta-analysis -13% elsewhere; LA Civic Center 2024 quote ~$8,148 per camera

name: Foot patrols on hot-spot blocks
caveat: Chains a Philadelphia crime effect with a New York price link; cost is salary + fringe only.
sources: Ratcliffe et al. 2011 (Philadelphia RCT): foot patrol -23% violent crime; LAPD officer salary + fringe ~$159k/yr (CAO 2025) | Schwartz, Susin & Voicu 2003 (NYC): 1% less violent crime -> +0.116% home prices

name: Violence interruption (GRYD-style)
caveat: GRYD is a comprehensive strategy; its effect is assigned to a local share of program cost.
sources: Brantingham, Tita & Herz 2021 (LA GRYD): violent crime ~-18% per reporting district (95% CI -3.5% to -33%; 625 districts); GRYD budget $41M/yr | Schwartz, Susin & Voicu 2003 (NYC): 1% less violent crime -> +0.116% home prices

name: Business improvement district (cleaning, ambassadors)
caveat: The LA estimate is for robbery; only robbery's share of violent crime is used.
sources: MacDonald et al. 2010 (30 LA BIDs): robbery -12% | Schwartz, Susin & Voicu 2003 (NYC): 1% less violent crime -> +0.116% home prices

name: Weekly litter and illegal-dumping cleanup
sources: MacDonald et al. 2026 street-cleaning RCT: litter -16%; LA CARE cleanup team ~$1.4M a year

name: Fast graffiti removal
sources: No causal price effect of graffiti removal found (sourcebook round 3); Gibbons 2004 links criminal damage to prices; LA graffiti crews $11.7M / 95 crews

name: Housing-first outreach for encampments
caveat: Assumes removing an encampment reverses the measured price discount.
sources: Bhandari 2024 (LA): encampments within 0.2 mi -> -1.41% sale prices; RAND Housing for Health: $30,458 per participant-year incl. county services

name: Rehab or replace blighted homes
caveat: Blighted homes inferred from Census vacancy, not identified properties.
sources: Ganduri & Maturana 2024: neighbors +2.3 pts after REO rehab; Rossi-Hansberg, Sarte & Owens 2010: $2-6 land value per $1

name: Affordable housing on underused land
caveat: Effects vary by neighborhood and can be negative in higher-income areas.
sources: Diamond & McQuade 2019: LIHTC +6.5% within 0.1 mi in low-income areas, -2.5% in high-income; LA HHH ~$597k per unit

name: Add a backyard home (ADU), owner-level
sources: Brueckner et al. 2024 (LA): ADU raises host parcel +9.2% (95% CI 6.6-11.9); Tanrisever 2025: neighbors -3% per +0.5 pt ADU density within 300 m; LA County median ADU cost $100k (2020)

name: Rooftop solar, owner-level
sources: Berkeley Lab 2015: ~$4/W premium for owned solar; DOE 2025 benchmark $2.95/W installed

name: Underground the overhead power lines
caveat: Canberra price association; private service connections and telecom work not included.
sources: LADWP 2019: $3.4M per circuit-mile in 2024 dollars undergrounding (contracts $2.2-4.5M); CPUC Rule 20: $1.8-6.1M/mile; LADWP overhead/underground line maps (NavigateLA); CAL FIRE hazard zones | McNair & Abelson 2010 (Canberra): underground power +2.9% house prices

name: EV fast-charging hub
caveat: The charger study is an association; 1% is a deep discount of its +3.3%.
sources: Liang et al. 2023 (14M California sales): +3.3% within 1 km of EV chargers; CARB 2025: 8-port DC fast site $800,473; AFDC: maintenance up to $400-800 per charger-year (electricity, network extra); federal AFDC station data

name: Solar + battery resilience hub
sources: LA County CPUC filing 2021: community microgrids $3.25-3.6M each

name: Freeway sound wall
caveat: OpenStreetMap maps few walls: check Caltrans before assuming a stretch is unprotected.
sources: Moretti & Wheeler 2025: new noise barrier +6.8% within 100 m; Caltrans soundwall costs

name: Freeway cap park (regional project, local share)
caveat: Shows this area's share; full cap cost and causal effect are uncertain.
sources: Klyde Warren Park cap $110M for 5 acres (2012); Hollywood Central Park proposal $250M + $780k a year | Crompton & Nicholls 2020 review: +8-10% adjacent to passive parks; small-park effect within ~100 m (Laszkiewicz 2022)

name: Air filters in classrooms near freeways
sources: Gilraine 2020 (LA, Porter Ranch): classroom air filters raised test scores

name: School modernization (bond-funded)
caveat: Uses this area's share of a modernization; bond effects are district-wide.
sources: Cellini, Ferreira & Rothstein 2010 (California school bonds): +6% prices; >= $1.50 home value per $1 of school capital

name: Library upgrade and longer hours
sources: Gilpin, Karger & Nencka: library capital spending +21% visits; no detectable home-price change; LA Benjamin Franklin branch renovation $5.5M

name: Community health clinic
sources: Bailey & Goodman-Bacon 2015: community health centers -2% mortality 50+; Via Care East LA clinic $38.8M (25,000 sq ft)

name: Attract a full grocery store
caveat: $2M is an incentive package, not the full cost of a store (private investment not counted).
sources: Worcester DiD: +7% within 400 m, +4% at 400-800 m after a grocery opens; Saengchote 2020: Whole Foods +6.7%

name: Main-street revival (facade grants, small-business help)
caveat: A retail-density association, not a measured effect of facade grants.
sources: Ghorbani & Meltzer 2024 (NYC): more nearby retail raises 1-4 family values, lowers condo values; Teh 2007 (LA): liquor stores raise nearby crime | MacDonald et al. 2010 (30 LA BIDs): robbery -12%

name: Outdoor dining and parklets
sources: SF Controller: parklet businesses +29% revenue; LA Al Fresco corridors +$12M sales

name: Weekly farmers market
caveat: Studies show an association with an inverted-U shape, not this exact effect.
sources: Farmers-market studies (Maryland 2020; Edmonton 2024): positive, inverted-U with distance

name: Allow more homes near transit (SB 79 / TOC zoning)
caveat: Policy change: public cost is planning only, so no per-dollar return is shown.
sources: Kuhlmann 2021 (Minneapolis): +3-5% affected single-family prices; Kestelman 2025 (LA TOC); HCD SB 79 (eff. July 2026)
